title: L1 comparative review record
description: One comparative L1 review (AES-V2.6 / SUE-564): a subject output compared pairwise against a relevant GOOD reference, never scored as one opaque number. Evidence spans are mandatory. tie and abstain are first-class outcomes. Integrity failures dominate stylistic wins — enforced by scripts/lib/l1-core.mjs, not merely stated. final_authority is always human: this record informs routing, it never grants publication or preference authority — see editorial/HITL-PROTOCOL.md, which stays the stronger authority.

dimensions.description: At minimum: thesis-worth, synthesis-independence, language-native-prose, formulaic-ai-shaped, audience-fit. Additional dimensions may be added; none of the required five may be omitted.

outcome.description: PASS, TIE, and ABSTAIN carry no rework. The four REWORK outcomes route into AES-V2.5's layer vocabulary via routes_to.

routes_to.description: Must be one of AES-V2.5's layer ids (editorial/feedback-routing.json), or null for PASS/TIE/ABSTAIN. Cross-checked against that table by scripts/lib/l1-core.mjs so the two packages cannot drift apart.

final_authority.description: Always human. L1 is advisory: it can recommend rework and it can recommend PASS, but it never accepts, publishes, or overrides an owner preference. See editorial/HITL-PROTOCOL.md and the may_not boundary in skills/review-l1/SKILL.md.

mode.description: pairwise is the default. tie and abstain are recorded here when no reference produced a decidable comparison at all, distinct from a per-dimension tie/abstain verdict.

references.description: The GOOD reference(s) compared against. Empty only when mode is abstain.

same_content_type.description: Whether every reference shares the subject's content_type. Compare like with like: Research to Research, News to News.

cross_cutting_dimension.description: Required when same_content_type is false. The only dimension genuinely cross-cutting enough to justify a cross-type reference, e.g. language-native-prose.

ref.description: A reference evaluation id, corpus entry id, or article id used as the comparison GOOD.

lineage_ref.description: Semantically required whenever provenance_class is "generated_output" — enforced by scripts/lib/l1-core.mjs, not this schema, because json-schema-lite has no conditional (if/then) keyword. Identifies the generation lineage so the anti-collapse rule can be evaluated; its absence no longer disables that rule (AES-V2 B5) — every reference_used being generated_output triggers anti-collapse regardless of lineage_ref.

anti_collapse.description: The anti-collapse rule: if every selected GOOD reference is a generated_output from the same lineage, the review must say so rather than silently treating the system's own prior outputs as an independent standard.

verdict.description: better/worse are relative to the reference. tie and abstain are first-class, never forced into a false preference.

evidence_span.description: A quoted sentence, named paragraph, or measured observation from the subject (and the reference, where relevant). Mandatory for every verdict, including tie: a verdict with no observable evidence is not a verdict. A genuine abstain still names what could not be observed.

integrity.description: Integrity failures dominate stylistic wins, always. A better-written piece that is less true loses.

evidence_span.description: Required whenever status is not clear.

evaluator.description: AES-V2 FIX (B7): full runtime lineage, not merely an evaluator kind. §7's model-drift contract requires L1's writer-facing counterpart — the reviewer — to be drift-detectable exactly like a renderer. Field names deliberately match visual-job.schema.json's `renderer`/`runtime` $defs.

agent.description: Present only when type is "agent". provider/model/model_version are required so a silent reviewer-model swap is detectable, never a transparent implementation detail.
